statement: [src] Every raised URI error message goes through `URI_ERROR`, which panics unless the URI was opened through `uri_open_optional` (the optional-resource path); only then does it print and return — a failed resolution can also return NULL with no message (UF4/UF5). [src] So a URI failure on an `efi` entry's `path:` is a panic (chainload.c 434-435), and the same panic path carries a hash mismatch under `hash_mismatch_panic: yes` (uri.c 301-305). [inf] The same is expected for `kernel_path:`/`module_path:`; their `uri_open` callers are listed in Limits, not opened.
quote: "// Only returns for an optional resource, which the caller then backs out of." (line 20)

statement: [src] After one leading `$` is dropped, the resource is compared with `strcmp` (case-sensitive) against `hdd`, `odd`, `boot`, `guid`, `uuid` (same dispatcher as `guid`), `fslabel`, `tftp`; any other name is "not valid" and goes to `URI_ERROR`, i.e. a panic for a required key.
host_value: [obs] all six URIs in `/boot/limine.conf` are `boot():/…` (r88 host receipt pin lines 30, 38, 50, 56, 64, 72)

statement: [src] `boot()` with an empty root opens the partition Limine booted from; `boot(N)` opens partition N (0-256, parsed with `strtoui`) on the SAME drive as the boot volume; N > 256 is a `URI_ERROR`; on a PXE boot `boot()` and `boot(N)` are redirected to `tftp` (lines 221-222, before the partition check). So `boot(N)` is resolvable by Limine — the gate's `LP-UNRESOLVED` for it is a gate limit (it hashes only `--esp`), not a Limine verdict.
host_value: [obs] no `boot(N)` on this host (UF2), so the limit does not fire here

statement: [src] `guid()`/`uuid()` parse the text mixed-endian first and retry big-endian; `fslabel()` looks a volume up by label; `hdd(d:p)`/`odd(d:p)` need a drive 1-256 (an omitted drive is a `URI_ERROR`) and a partition 0-256. A volume that is simply not found returns NULL with no message of its own; the caller decides what that means (UF5).
quote: "URI_ERROR(\"Drive number cannot be omitted for hdd():/ and odd():/\");" (line 119)

statement: [src] An `efi` entry (`protocol: efi`, `chainload()`) reads `PATH`, then `IMAGE_PATH`; if `uri_open` returns NULL — file absent, volume not found, or a value `uri_resolve` cannot split (no `(` or no `):/`, which returns false without a message, lines 46-63) — Limine panics with "Failed to open image". So `LP-MISSING`, an unresolvable volume, and a URI-less `path:` value are all a panic of that entry at boot, not an ignored line.
quote: "panic(true, \"efi: Failed to open image with path `%s`. Is the path correct?\", image_path);" (line 435)
host_value: [obs] all six entries are `protocol: efi` (host receipt lines 29, 37, 49, 55, 63, 71)

statement: [src] Around that `uri_open`, `chainload()` sets `secure_boot_active = false` and restores it after; inside `uri_open` that flag gates only the "Secure Boot is active and URI has no associated hash" error. So an `efi` entry's `path:` may be unhashed under Secure Boot (the firmware's LoadImage verifies the image instead), while a pin that IS present is still compared (the mismatch path does not read the flag). The code comment says Limine "does not need to enforce its own hash check here"; the code only waives the missing-hash rule. Under Secure Boot, menu.c also forces `hash_mismatch_panic` on (menu.c 1714-1717), so a present-pin mismatch there is a `URI_ERROR` panic, not the Y-prompt.
quote: "// The firmware's LoadImage will verify the Secure Boot signature of the chainloaded EFI application, so Limine does not need" (lines 423-424)

statement: [src] Every panic above is `panic(true, …)`: it prints `PANIC`, then "Press a key to return to menu", and the menu comes back, so another entry (a snapshot entry, the fallback) can be chosen — on UEFI only while the firmware's boot services are still up (`efi_boot_services_exited == false`, lines 71-77), which holds for a path that fails to open. Under measured boot the menu return is refused and the machine prints "System halted." (UEFI; a BIOS build prints a CTRL+ALT+DEL line instead). Measured boot is on only when the config says exactly `measured_boot: yes` or Secure Boot is active, and is forced off when the firmware exposes no TPM/CC measurement interface. Limine's "Secure Boot active" is itself narrower than the firmware flag: `init_config` clears it when no config checksum is enrolled (config.c 488-492). Narrowing from wave seat ScoutSources (SR11, SR18, SR21).
quote: "print(\"Press a key to return to %s.\", booting_from_editor ? \"editor\" : \"menu\");" (panic.s2.c line 78)
host_value: [obs] no `measured_boot` key in `/boot/limine.conf`; Secure Boot off; `/sys/class/tpm/` empty

statement: [inf] On this host, therefore: the gate's `not-modelled` rows cannot come from a resource (every URI is `boot():/`), and an `LP-MISSING` main `path:` would be a panic that returns to the menu after a key press — the snapshot entries and `EFI fallback` stay selectable. The round-86 incident's mismatches stay `prompt` (`hash_mismatch_panic: no`, r87 LP5). Measured boot is off here whatever the firmware's TPM state: the config has no `measured_boot` key and Secure Boot is off (UF7's two switches). The firmware's TPM protocol was not probed; an empty `/sys/class/tpm/` is a Linux-side signal only and does not answer `tpm_present()` (wave seat ScoutSources SR4). Not executed at boot.
